title: HBG Delivery Get Well
purpose: The Delivery side of Homebody Guaranty: what happens after a resident is enrolled. Scheduled charges that match the policy, cancellations that reverse their own charges, policies that stay in sync with Leap, claims, and the reporting the agency and Finance need. The escalated clients feel this side as refund requests. HBG Distribution Get Well covers the Sign side (application, renewals, transfers). Economics for the line live on Insurance Line Performance.

sections.title: What HBG is wrapping
sections.body: HBG embeds Leap's Guarantor Waiver Program. In Leap's native version the recurring Guarantor Waiver Fee on the resident's scheduled charges is the policy: it enrolls, keeps, and renews coverage, and Leap invoices the property for every fee it sees each month, whole months, no proration. Leap tells property teams to audit charge codes monthly, audit recent transfers, watch a Flagged Cancellations tab for dropped charges and move-outs, and file claims within 120 days. HBG's promise is to do those audits inside Entrata's lease and ledger events. Each category below is one of those audits, automated imperfectly.

sections.title: Delivery-side issue categories
rows: Scheduled charges and billing

Residents charged more than once a month, wrong amounts, premiums changing on their own, charges missing on active policies, enrollment fee posting twice or not at all. Because Leap invoices the property off these same charges, every ledger error is also a property invoice error.

64 issues, 34 open (summary mentions charge, fee, premium, pricing, or amount). DEV-349211, DEV-335646, DEV-349177, DEV-349205, DEV-347186, DEV-336584. A dedicated request tracker opened 2026-10-09 (DEV-347150).
Monthly charge-code audit: pull recurring charges and tie them to lease dates.

Cancellations, refunds, reinstatement

Cancel before policy start does not reverse posted charges. Reversing future charges on cancellation has been in development since April. Flat-cancel on Leap's confirm is new and unstarted. Reinstatement and cancel/rewrite epics have sat in New since June. Refund requests arrive as R&D bugs and close by datafix.
20 cancel or reversal issues (10 open) plus 12 refund or reinstatement requests (4 open). DEV-286241, DEV-336247, DEV-349261, DEV-349465, DEV-303585, DEV-303584, DEV-343499.
Flagged Cancellations tab: property cancels, files a claim, or fixes the charge. Cancellations are final.

Policy issuance and Leap sync

Migrations that succeed on Leap's side and fail on ours, leaving partial records. Issuance pulling the wrong lease interval. confirmed_on not syncing. Rate sync delay. Policy term not matching lease term. A 10-policy batch ceiling on migration.
42 issues, 24 open (summary mentions migration, E2E, L2E, PDM, sync, confirm, Leap, or interval). DEV-338721, DEV-350065, DEV-344074, DEV-349445, DEV-336331, DEV-342834, DEV-334131, DEV-287713.

Thin, because claims live in Leap's portal. Entrata's exposure is the policy UI, a load failure on claim submission, cancel-claim, and renewal blocking when a claim is open or paid.

sections.title: Get-well checklist, from Jira status on 2026-10-19

items.text: Recurring and enrollment charge reversal is a defined product function, not a datafix (DEV-343499).
Flat cancellation on Leap policy confirm reverses resident billing on the collapsed term (DEV-349261, DEV-349465).
Cancel, rewrite, and coverage change are workflows (DEV-303584).
E2E migrations cannot create duplicate DA/HBG charges (DEV-336299).
Leap migration status is recalculated with recovery actions when a write is interrupted (DEV-323454).
HB Guaranty Reporting has a release (DEV-138646).
Invoices say Homebody Guaranty, not DepositInsure (BIL-591).
Renewal process documented for clients, CS, and Service (Track 6).

sections.title: Where the line is with HBG Distribution Get Well
sections.body: Distribution owns getting the resident enrolled and re-enrolled: application and screening, renewal offers and repricing, transfers, and the lease documents that price the guaranty. Delivery owns everything the policy does after that: the charges it posts, how it cancels and refunds, whether it matches what Leap has, claims, and reporting. A transfer that creates no new policy is Distribution. A transfer that double-bills is Delivery. When one ticket is both, it goes where the fix is.
